_comment: CI run 37608671586 / job 112750669255: DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 FP4 on 8x MI355X, TP8/EP8 with DP attention, concurrency 128, DSpark + MegaMoE/EPLB + HiCache. A different stack from agentx_glm52 in every way that matters to kernel selection: the MoE path is MegaMoE with EPLB expert migration rather than a fused MXFP4 MoE, attention is Opus MLA v4, and 19% of device time sits in peer-to-peer dispatch/combine rather than in GEMM.

target._note_image: The declared image is the recipe tag the CI run named. It was overwritten upstream at 14:49 UTC on 2026-10-07, after the CI job finished at 12:57 UTC, so the tag now resolves to sha256:65c5a944... carrying SGLang 1e86143bf0 rather than the CI source. Every run against this config therefore executes a locally derived image rebuilt from the CI pip record; byte identity with the historical image is unprovable and is never claimed. See stages.baseline.params.runtime_image.

params._note_skill: adopt, not ci-run-replay. Two reasons, both specific to this CI run. (1) There is no historical digest to pin: the recipe tag was overwritten after the job finished, so ci-run-replay's first gate -- an image addressed by digest, present locally -- could only be satisfied by a digest of a locally derived image, which proves repeatability but not identity with CI. (2) This site's harness splits host side (run_host.py, which creates its own container) from container side (in_container.py); ci-run-replay creates the container itself, so driving run_host.py through it would nest containers. The receipt adopted here is a full reproduction of exactly this job measured on 2026-10-13 -- 2935.11997 tok/s against CI 2982.36554, -1.584%, 10986 successful requests, 0 errors, submission_valid, the original CI result processor re-run on the original raw records. The guarantee ci-run-replay exists to give -- both arms measured on one machine -- is supplied here by applyback instead, which measures its own reference leg rather than differencing against this number.
params._note_drift: -1.584% against CI is inside max_reference_drift but is not noise: 118 physical cores locally against 128 in CI, plus a derived image. It is the floor this campaign's gain is measured from, not a number to be improved by re-running.

params.selection: per-phase Top 5 AND overall GPU-time share > 3%
params._note_prior: A partial run of this same skill (SKILL.md md5-identical to the vendored copy) already produced the census, the ranking, the selection and the boundary declarations for this exact CI run: 326 kernels, 4,326,042 launches, 8 targets, 6 declared task boundaries. Its tasks/ hold kernel_src/ and nothing else -- no cases.py, no meta.json, no unittest.py, no captures, no oracles -- so section 4 is substantively unstarted. Sections 1-3 are imported with their provenance rather than recomputed from the same traces.
params._note_scope: Ranking is deployment-scope (all 8 ranks), not rank 0. Rank 0 and rank 3 agree on only 3 of their 10 top targets, so a single-rank ranking would select a different kernel set from the same run.

params._note_budget: 12 h per unit test. With 6 task boundaries on 8 GPUs every task owns a GPU for the whole window, so 12 h per test is also 12 h wall-clock.
params._note_amdahl: GPU busy fraction is 98.31%, so device time bounds the step -- but TP8/EP8 synchronises every rank each step, so a step shortens only by the *minimum* per-rank saving. A kernel sped up on one rank and not another buys nothing end to end.

params._note_harness: harness_cmd/case_file are null because this harness has no case table and no python_overlay hook: run_host.py launches the container and in_container.py launches the frozen server CLI. Wiring applyback means giving it that hook, and that is a stage-skill change, not a config value. Until it exists this stage reports blocked rather than measuring the candidate through a different client than the reference.
params._note_reference: reference_run is null so both arms are measured here, on one node, by one harness. The adopted baseline was measured on node053 under a job that has since ended; differencing a candidate on another node against it would attribute the node difference to the kernels.
